title: Architecture & Standards: Unified Guidelines and ADRs
author: Amina K. Patel
body:
Summary:
This consolidated guidance captures Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also catalogs the active Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) that govern major design trade-offs. Apply these standards for all new services, significant refactors, and public-facing SDK/API changes.

Audience:
- Service owners, platform engineers, SREs, and SDK authors
- Reviewers and approvers for ADRs and API changes

Principles (high level):
1. Developer ergonomics first: APIs and SDKs should be predictable, well-documented, and backward-compatible where possible.
2. Production-grade defaults: sensible SLOs, observability, and secure-by-default configs.
3. Measurable economics: design decisions should include expected cost/latency trade-offs.
4. Incremental rollout: prefer canary/A-B rollouts and automated fallback for risk reduction.

Sections:
1) API standards
Purpose: ensure consistent surface area across Redwood public and internal APIs to reduce client errors and simplify SDK maintenance.
Mandates:
- Versioning: Use semantic versioning for public REST endpoints and explicit model-version query param for inference routes (e.g., ?model=redwood-v1.3).
- Request/response schema: always return stable JSON schema with top-level keys: {"request_id","status","data","meta"}.
- Errors: follow RFC 7807 problem+json structure. Include error_code string and retryable boolean in "meta.error".
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination with opaque next_cursor.
- Rate limiting: responses to 429 must include "Retry-After" header and a machine-readable quota-type in meta.
- Authentication: Bearer tokens (short lived) for hosted APIs; mutual TLS for private deployments where configured.
- Backcompat policy: additive changes only by minor releases. Breaking changes require 6 weeks deprecation notice and opt-in header.

API checklist (PR template):
- [ ] API contract YAML/JSON included in repo
- [ ] Example SDK usage in at least one language (Python/Node)
- [ ] Automated contract tests included (contract-tests/*)
- [ ] API doc page updated
- [ ] ADR created if change impacts cross-team compatibility

2) Coding standards
Purpose: maintain readable, testable, and operable code across services.
Language-specific guidelines (summary):
- Python: follow PEP8; use type hints (mypy strictness level = basic); require black + ruff in pre-commit.
- Go: gofmt + go vet required; prefer small interfaces; avoid generics for public packages unless necessary.
- Rust/C++ (runtime components): document unsafe blocks and include safety rationale.

Common standards:
- Tests: unit coverage target >= 80% for libraries, >= 60% for services. CI must run unit and integration tests on PRs.
- Linting: configured in CI as failing job.
- Dependency management: use dependency scanning (Snyk/OSS scanning) and require security approval for new infra libraries.
- Secrets: never check secrets; use org secret-store; rotate keys every 90 days for long-lived service keys.

3) Infrastructure standards
Ownership: eng-infra maintains core modules. Service owners must use standard IaC modules where practical.
Network/security:
- VPCs: production services must be deployed to environment-specific VPCs with private subnets for runtime nodes.
- Ingress: all external-facing endpoints go through API Gateway + WAF.
- IAM: least privilege; automated role generation via infra modules.
Provisioning
- Terraform modules: deploy using canonical modules under infra/terraform/modules. Changes to shared modules require an ADR and cross-team review.
- Immutable infra: prefer immutable artifacts and blue-green or canary deploys.

Capacity planning and GPU fleet:
- Tagging: GPU instances must be tagged with pool, region, and instance-class.
- Autoscaling policy: minimum pool size = steady-state throughput / model_tps_estimate * safety_factor(1.2).
- Cost guardrails: monitor per-pool burn rate; automatic scaling down if 72h burn exceeds forecast by >15% without approval.

4) Model-serving standards
Scope: inference runtime and deployment of model artifacts.
Model packaging:
- Artifact format: ONNX or TorchScript for internal runtime; include metadata.json with schema: {"model_name","version","supported_inputs","max_seq_len","quantization_profile"}.
- Size limits: artifact packages for hosted must be <= 40GB; larger artifacts require dedicated capacity justification.
Serving contracts:
- Input validation: runtime must reject malformed requests with 400 and provide request_id.
- Backpressure: where queue length > 1000 or estimated tail latency exceeds SLO, return 503 + Retry-After and trigger autoscaling event.
- Fallbacks: every public inference route must support an automatic fallback policy in routing config (higher latency cheaper model / region failover).
Observability hooks:
- Emit model_version, shard_id, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size to tracing and metrics for every request.

Model lifecycle and rollouts:
- Canary: 1% traffic for 24 hours, then 10% for 48 hours before full rollout.
- Quality checks: automated eval suite must run on canary traffic and report any metric regressions beyond thresholds.
- Rollback: automated rollback on >25% increase in error rate or >20% regression in quality metrics (as defined by model-specific tests).

5) Observability standards
Goals: detect, triage, and debug production issues quickly while keeping operational cost reasonable.
Metrics:
- Every service must emit: request_count, error_count, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, cpu_usage, memory_usage.
- Inference-specific: tokens_generated, tokens_cost_usd, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate.
Tracing:
- Distributed traces with 200ms sampling for production, 100% sampling for errors. Include request_id and model_version as span tags.
Logging:
- Structured JSON logs, severity levels, include request_id and shard_id.
- Log retention: default 30 days for dev/staging, 90 days for production, configurable by compliance.
Alerting:
- Alert types: latency (p95 > SLO), error rate (> SLO threshold), capacity (queue length), infrastructure (instance CPU/memory).
- Alerts must include suggested runbook link and on-call owner.

6) Performance standards and SLOs
Default SLOs (hosted API inference):
- Availability: 99.95% (monthly)
- Latency SLOs by route (examples):
  - small-text-generation (short prompts, <128 tokens): p50 < 40ms, p95 < 200ms
  - chat-completion (context up to 1024 tokens): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 400ms
  - embeddings (batchable): p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms
- Error budget: 0.05% (monthly)
- Cost-per-token targets: tracked per-model and reported to cost dashboards; recommended TTL for caching and batching configured per-route.
Performance testing:
- Benchmark harness: use eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Include realistic prompt mixes, sequence length distributions, and concurrency patterns.
- Regression policy: any change that increases median latency by >10% or p95 by >15% requires an ADR with mitigation plan.

7) ADRs (Architecture Decision Records)
Purpose: capture and communicate long-lived architecture decisions.
ADR format (required fields):
- adr_id (e.g., ADR-2026-012)
- title
- status (proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated)
- date
- context
- decision
- consequences
- owners
- related_pages

Active ADRs (summary):
- ADR-2025-034: "Model artifact format: ONNX-first" — accepted 2025-09-01. Decision: prefer ONNX for cross-runtime compatibility; Rust runtime keeps TorchScript bridge. Owners: Runtime team.
- ADR-2025-072: "API error contract: RFC7807" — accepted 2025-11-11. Decision: adopt problem+json with error_code and retryable. Owners: API team.
- ADR-2026-002: "Inference fallback policy" — accepted 2026-01-22. Decision: require automatic model fallback and region failover for hosted endpoints. Owners: Routing & Serving teams.

ADR process (how to propose and accept):
1. Author creates ADR draft in docs/adr with proposed decision and alternatives.
2. Add reviewers (owner_team and at least two cross-team reviewers).
3. Run 7-day comment period; collect engineering and product signoff.
4. If no blocking feedback, ADR status -> accepted and add to confluence index.
5. For urgent changes, use expedited 48-hour review with explicit justification.

Example ADR template (text):
---
adr_id: ADR-YYYY-NNN
title: Short descriptive title
status: proposed
date: YYYY-MM-DD
context: |
  Background and constraints.
decision: |
  The chosen architecture/standard and rationale.
consequences: |
  Operational, cost, compatibility consequences.
owners: |
  Team: Person A, Person B
related_pages: |
  /confluence/architecture-and-standards/....
---

8) Change management and deprecation windows
- Minor changes: non-breaking additions — no formal ADR, but require API contract tests and doc updates.
- Breaking changes: must create an ADR and a deprecation plan with at least 6 weeks notice for public APIs and 2 weeks for internal-only endpoints.

9) Ownership and runbooks
- Each standard above has an owning team and a primary contact. The consolidated owner list is maintained in the directory: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/owners-index.
- Every alert must link to a runbook and a primary on-call owner. Runbooks must be tested in game-days at least twice annually.

Appendix: Quick reference tables
SLO quick reference (hosted inference):
+--------------------------------+---------------------+---------------------+
| route                          | p50                 | p95                 |
+--------------------------------+---------------------+---------------------+
| embeddings (batchable)         | < 30ms              | < 120ms             |
| small-text-generation (<128)   | < 40ms              | < 200ms             |
| chat-completion (<=1024)       | < 80ms              | < 400ms             |
+--------------------------------+---------------------+---------------------+

Sample rollout steps (model serving):
1. Build and package model (include metadata.json).
2. Upload to artifact registry; run pre-deploy validations (size, signature).
3. Create canary deploy (1% traffic) and enable tracing and evals.
4. Monitor automated metrics for 24h (latency, error, eval-quality).
5. Expand to 10% for 48h; if stable, complete rollout.
6. If thresholds breached, rollback to previous version and open incident.

Contacts and escalation:
- Architecture owner: Priya Raman (architecture-and-standards) — priya@redwood.example.com
- Runtime lead: Marcus Nguyen (eng-serving-runtime)
- Eng-infra lead: Diego Morales
